title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has released its response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining how it plans to address AI governance and public concerns. It emphasizes commitments to improve transparency, oversight, and responsible AI use while proposing specific steps for developing and enforcing standards.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee and set rules for using artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications. The guide aims to protect fairness, reliability and transparency in assessments while supporting innovation in the education sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report evaluates how AI systems use copyrighted works and examines the legal and ethical implications of that use. It offers recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to address the challenges and opportunities raised by the committee. It details new policies, regulatory measures and collaborative initiatives aimed at promoting responsible AI development while protecting public interests and maintaining economic competitiveness.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, including clear guidelines on its tasks and decision‑making process. It also answers common questions about the review, explaining how the committee will assess AI’s impact on public policy to ensure accountability and transparency.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines key concerns and recommendations for responsible AI development and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence will reshape rules for medical products, ensuring safety while encouraging innovation. It applies the AI White Paper's principles to guide regulators in overseeing AI-driven medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy declares that the country aims to be the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defense organization in AI for its size. It outlines plans for adopting, governing, and developing AI capabilities to improve overall defense effectiveness.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to make the most of AI opportunities while carefully controlling risks. It outlines strategies for collaboration, development of standards, and risk‑mitigation measures to ensure AI benefits the public safely.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report outlines how copyright-protected works are currently being used to train and develop AI systems, explaining that the data handling follows the rules set out in Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made so far, notes any gaps or challenges, and recommends steps to improve compliance and ensure fair use of copyrighted material.
